title: A tracked allocator
description:
Count every allocation in a program and report leaks with where they came from.

```
alloc 64 bytes  (loadLevel)
alloc 128 bytes (spawnEnemy)
free  64 bytes
leaks at exit: 1 block, 128 bytes, allocated in spawnEnemy
peak: 192 bytes
```
hints: A `std::map<void*, Block>` stores one `Block` per pointer. `g_blocks[p] = Block{ size, where };` adds or replaces an entry; `auto it{ g_blocks.find(p) };` finds one (`it == g_blocks.end()` means not there, otherwise `it->second` is the `Block`); `g_blocks.erase(it);` removes it; and `for (const auto& [ptr, block] : g_blocks)` visits every entry.
Keep a running total and the peak, updated in both functions (lesson 2.09).
A macro `#define ALLOC(n) trackedAlloc(n, __func__)` fills in the function name for you.
requirements: `void* trackedAlloc(std::size_t size, const char* where)` and `void trackedFree(void* p)`.
A map from pointer to `(size, where)`; freeing an unknown pointer is reported.
A report of live blocks and the peak total.
stretch: Run the leaking version under AddressSanitizer and compare its report with yours.
